subject: ACME - post-call: integration & model-routing next steps
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
To: Sofia Reyes <sofia.reyes@acme.com>, Paul Chen <paul.chen@acme.com>
Cc: Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>, Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 22 Jul 2026 14:03:00 -0700
Subject: ACME - post-call: integration & model-routing next steps

Thanks again for taking the time today — great conversation. Quick recap and proposed next steps for the integration / architecture follow-up we discussed: 

1) SDK & auth: ACME will try the Node + Python SDKs (we'll share the integration guide). You mentioned the app uses service-to-service calls from a backend pool; recommended pattern is API key + request scoping, and for private deployments we can demo KMS integration.

2) Routing & policies: we covered latency-based routing for low-latency search, cost-tier routing for batch generation, and a fallback chain: fast low-cost model -> region fallback -> high-cost low-latency model. Marcus will sketch a YAML policy proposal.

3) Structured output & tool-calling: we recommend using our function-calling + structured-output schema for the invoice-extraction pipeline; embeddings + reranker to improve top-k relevance for search.

4) Next steps (owners):
 - Marissa: share integration guide & contract overview (EOD tomorrow)
 - Dev: provide example SDK auth pattern + sample code (by Fri)

From: Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>, Sofia Reyes <sofia.reyes@acme.com>, Paul Chen <paul.chen@acme.com>
Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>, Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 23 Jul 2026 09:18:00 -0700
Subject: Re: ACME - post-call: integration & model-routing next steps

Thanks Marissa — noted. A couple of quick technical clarifications from my side after looking at ACME's app notes: 

- Auth: for your backend pool the recommended flow is short-lived scoped API keys minted from your control plane. If you need HSM/KMS we can map to our private deployment option; otherwise API keys + IP allowlist should be fine.

- SDK setup: attaching a minimal sample that shows Node startup, streaming, and function-calling. (Attachment: redwood-sdk-integration-guide.pdf)

- Embeddings/re-ranker: to avoid double-cost on large corpora, we should do periodic offline embedding generation + a per-call lightweight reranker. I can drop a small script and a reranker config.

Questions for ACME: what's your 95th pct latency requirement for the invoice-extraction UI? That will determine whether we push to a low-latency variant in the routing policy.

— Dev
Senior Solutions Engineer
Redwood Inference

From: Sofia Reyes <sofia.reyes@acme.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
Cc: Paul Chen <paul.chen@acme.com>, Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 23 Jul 2026 13:45:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: ACME - post-call: integration & model-routing next steps

Thanks both — this is helpful. For the invoice UI our internal SLA target is 300ms P95 for the quick preview (first 1–2 lines) and up to 1.5s for full extraction.

A few priorities for us:
- Keep cost predictable for batch processing overnight (we run ~10k docs nightly).
- Region routing: we need EU region support for EU customers; fallback to US only if EU capacity constrained.

Marcus, Jonas — looping you for the infra questions: can we start with the hosted API and then migrate to dedicated pools if latency or data isolation becomes an issue?

Sofia
Staff Product Manager, ACME Corp

From: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>
To: Sofia Reyes <sofia.reyes@acme.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>, Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.com>
Cc: Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 24 Jul 2026 10:02:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: ACME - post-call: integration & model-routing next steps

Sofia — good notes. Yes, starting on hosted API is common; we can stage a Dedicated migration plan with reserved capacity once you hit predictable load or need stricter isolation. I'll draft a model-routing + policy YAML that encodes:

- route by latency objective: P95 <= 300ms -> model: redwood-llama-lowlat-v2
- otherwise use redwood-llama-cost-quantized for batch jobs
- fallback chain: same-region variant -> cross-region (EU->US) -> high-availability small model
- embedding jobs: route to batch pool with quantized weights and autoscale for nightly runs

I'll attach a first-pass YAML and include annotations for cost impact. (Attachment: acme-model-routing-proposal.yaml)

Marcus
Principal Solutions Architect, Redwood Inference

From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
To: Sofia Reyes <sofia.reyes@acme.com>, Paul Chen <paul.chen@acme.com>
Cc: Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>, Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.com>
Date: Sat, 25 Jul 2026 09:12:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: ACME - post-call: integration & model-routing next steps

Appreciate the quick turnaround, team. Action items for this week: 
- Marissa: send contract summary & SOW skeleton (EOD Mon) — will include Dedicated migration pricing options.
- Dev: share SDK auth sample + short script for embedding/reranker (Mon) — attached guide has the basics.
- Marcus: review the YAML in the attachment and highlight any hard constraints for the EU->US fallback (cost and compliance notes).
- ACME: confirm whether 300ms P95 is a hard requirement for launch or a target (Sofia)

I'll book a follow-up for next Tue to review the routing YAML and the SDK samples — propose Jul 28 10:00am PT. Reply with availability and I’ll send the invite.

Thanks — looking forward to progressing this.

— Marissa
